title: The prop bar is an EXPECTED-VALUE question, not a drawdown-avoidance one — and the corpus cannot answer it
note: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-22, and it REPLACES the bar I proposed an hour earlier: 'it's ok if there is ever breach, the idea is that we want to promote strategies that create a portfolio that we would statistically expect to produce a profit (over the initial account cost of about 1%) before the account dies - that is the basis for building the prop portfolio.' [!] SO THE PROP BAR IS: E[profit before the account dies] > the account cost. Breach is an ACCEPTED, EXPECTED outcome -- the cost of the bet -- not a failure to prevent. This is a ruin-WITH-PAYOFF problem and the quantity is a survival-weighted expected value. [!] I PROPOSED `max_dd_r < 4.0` AS THE PROP BAR AND THAT IS WITHDRAWN. It is a risk-avoidance constraint on a problem that is not about avoiding risk, and it would have refused exactly the high-variance legs this account exists to buy a lottery ticket on. [!] AND MY SUPPORTING ARGUMENT WAS ALSO WRONG, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL CORRECTION: I said 1.5% sizing against a 6% static DD 'makes almost nothing fit'. THE BARRIER RATIO IS INVARIANT TO SIZING. At risk_pct 1.5: DD room 6%/1.5% = 4.0R, profit target 10%/1.5% = 6.67R, ratio 1.667. At 0.5%: 12.0R and 20.0R, ratio 1.667. Both barriers scale together, so cutting risk_pct does not change the ratio at all; it helps only through the second-order effect that more trades to either barrier let positive drift accumulate against variance. With trend_donchian_eth_prop's expectancy of +0.042R/trade, +6.67R is ~159 trades of drift against 4R of room, so variance dominates heavily -- whether smaller sizing raises P(success) is a COMPUTABLE QUESTION and I should not have asserted it in either direction. [!] TWO FEATURES OF THIS ACCOUNT MAKE THE EV BETTER THAN A NAIVE ABSORBING-BARRIER MODEL, both CONFIRMED in config/prop_rulesets/breakout.yaml: (1) drawdown_type is STATIC -- 'off the STARTING balance; NOT trailing and NOT locked/raised on payout' -- so every dollar of profit is PERMANENT cushion and the account gets monotonically safer as it wins; survival is front-loaded. (2) min_trading_days 0 and max_eval_days null -- no time pressure, can clear in one trade, so there is no forced-pace term. STRUCTURE: $45 (0.9% of the $5,000 account) buys a shot at +10% ($500) before -6% ($300); clearing converts to a funded account paying 80/20 on subsequent profits under the same static limits. So E[value] = P(clear eval) x E[lifetime payout | funded] - $45. [!] SELECTION CRITERION, AND IT IS NOT net_R: maximise P(reaching the target before the floor). A leg with LOWER expectancy but tighter loss clustering beats a higher-expectancy leg whose losses arrive in lumps. And it is a PORTFOLIO question, not a per-leg one -- legs whose drawdowns are uncorrelated smooth the path to the barrier. [!] NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH R8: the operator chose NO concentration cap for bybit_2, and correlation is nonetheless load-bearing HERE, in the opposite direction -- on prop it is not a risk limit, it is the mechanism that raises P(survival). [!] THIS RETROACTIVELY EXPLAINS THE _prop EXIT GEOMETRY, which nobody wrote down: tp_r 6.0 vs 50.0, trail_mult 3.5 vs 5.0, stale_exit_bars 12, trail_decay_stall_bars 10 / tight_mult 1.8. Capping the upside at 6R and cutting dead trades is exactly what raises P(hit +6.67R before -4R) at the cost of expectancy. Someone built the right thing for the right reason and recorded neither, so it read as an arbitrary divergence between prop and bybit -- which is what the operator asked about today. [!] THE ACTUAL GAP IS A MISSING MEASUREMENT, NOT A MISSING CONSTRAINT: MEASURED 2026-09-22, none of the 52 records under comms/strategy_evidence/ carries a per-trade R series or ANY path statistic (keys are basis, config_fingerprint, cost_stack, coverage_state, decision_rule, expectancy_r_oos, fold_detail, folds, folds_positive, n_trades_oos, net_r_oos, net_r_oos_fee_only, omitted_levers, param_selection_provenance, window_days -- no drawdown of any kind), and scripts/ci/check_roster_promotion_evidence.py never reads one. fold_detail gives only a per-fold SUM over months, which is not an equity path. DELIVERABLE: emit the per-trade OOS R series (or a sufficient path summary) so P(target before floor) is computable per leg AND per candidate portfolio, then register that rule BEFORE using it. [!] WHAT I COMPUTED FROM fold_detail AND ITS LIMIT, kept because it is what prompted the reframe: 13 of the 42 legs with fold detail have a single fold worse than -4R, and BOTH legs live on breakout_1 are among them while both are marked `pass` (trend_donchian_eth_prop worst fold -5.3884R on total +7.13). That is NOT evidence of a breach -- a fold's net_R is a sum over months, not a contiguous drawdown -- and under this row's bar it would not be disqualifying even if it were. It is evidence only that the bar cannot see the path. | 2026-09-27 (lane session_013wNhAh3Z3EPTFyJuANcRrz, branch claude/w6-prop-ev): THE TOOL EXISTS. scripts/research/prop_ev_sim.py (+ tests/test_prop_ev_sim.py, --self-test). Monte-Carlo of ONE Breakout $5k account life: shared balance across legs with OVERLAPPING trades, daily loss on intraday equity vs the 00:30-UTC balance, static DD off start, eval->fresh funded account after a 1-day approval gap, bank-everything-above-start payouts (14d then weekly, 80%), rebuy via renewal-reward. Breakout costs recomputed per trade from gross_r/entry/sl: 8 bps commission + 3 bps slippage + 0.033%/day swap per 00:00-UTC crossing. Intra-trade path unseen, so reported under 4 marks: realized (optimistic), path (hourly Brownian bridge conditioned on the stop and the recorded MFE = the central estimate), bridge and stop (pessimistic bounds). EV CI = outer block bootstrap of the evidence history (100 re-drawn histories x 200 lives). POSITIVE CONTROL: gambler's ruin P(pass) 0.378 vs analytic 0.375 (p=.5) and 0.733 vs 0.732 (p=.6), E[trades to absorption] 15.12 vs 15. INPUT SCHEMA for P2 (JSONL per trade): entry_time, exit_time + either {gross_r, entry, sl} (--costs breakout) or {net_r} (--costs as_given); optional leg, mfe_r. [!] B6's 'barrier ratio is invariant to sizing' is right for the barriers and misses the discreteness: at 1.0% two stops are 2.14% < 3%. Path EV by risk_pct: 1.5% -$12 / 1.0% +$173 (CI -$23..+$797, P(pass) 0.56) / 0.75% +$213 / 0.5% +$260 (17% of lives still alive at the 730-day horizon, scored at banked only, so understated). EV PER YEAR with rebuy: 1.0% +$604, 0.75% +$415, 0.5% +$242. Fewer, longer lives at lower size, so per-year EV peaks near 1.0% on this grid. [!] Also correcting this row's own note: 'every dollar of profit is PERMANENT cushion' is FALSE in the funded phase under the operator's bank-ASAP withdrawal policy (breakout.yaml withdrawal_policy above_start): profit is withdrawn weekly and the floor stays at $4,700, so the cushion resets to $300 every payout. It holds only within the eval and between payouts. [!] DECISION FOR THE OPERATOR (Tier-3, NOT taken, NOT proposed as a config diff by this lane): breakout_1 risk_pct 1.5% vs 1.0% (config/prop_rulesets/breakout_routing.yaml risk_pct + accounts.yaml breakout_1.risk.risk_pct). The measurement says 1.0% moves the central EV from about -$10 to about +$173 per $45 account on the same evidence. Caveat: n=234 trades over one year, so every CI still straddles 0 at its p5.
